intro: If you're after a place to stay in Ratchaburi that's cheap, cute and designed with style, and comes with free parking for a night or two before you head out to make merit at the temples, see the dragon jars, or stop by a floating market — The Sun Resort Ratchaburi is a small boutique resort that opened back in 2021 in Don Tako, Mueang Ratchaburi · what people talk about most is the loft-themed rooms that look smarter than the price suggests, ranging from doubles with a large bed and mountain-view rooms to an 8-bed dorm for groups of friends or backpackers · there's a garden, a terrace, free bikes to borrow, and Wi-Fi that plenty of guests praise as fast · prices start at around THB 550–700/night · it scored 8.4 on Trip.com and 7.7 from 405 reviews on Booking.com

body.html: The Sun Resort Ratchaburi overview — who it suits — to put it as plainly as possible, The Sun Resort Ratchaburi is a small boutique resort in the "cute and designed for an easy price" lane rather than a luxury resort with every facility · it's a 2-star place that only opened in 2021, sitting in Don Tako, Mueang Ratchaburi, a little way out of the city center in an area that's still quiet · its position is clear: a small resort that leans on loft-themed and themed rooms that look better than the price, plus a garden and a small terrace to sit out on · from real reviews, the people it suits best are couples who want a cute, budget-friendly stay, travelers driving their own car who need free parking, groups of friends or backpackers looking for a cheap dorm, and anyone stopping over for one night before moving on · if you're after a swimming pool, a gym, a large dining room, or full hotel-style service, you'll want to set your expectations to match what this place actually is, because The Sun plays the role of a small resort selling charm through design and value, not luxury or a full slate of facilities · put simply, if you want a clean, cutely styled bed, easy parking and a bill in the hundreds of baht, this place does that job well at a price that's hard to find in town — but if you're coming to "spend the whole day relaxing" using the resort facilities as your main activity, there may be better options in the province

Location and getting around — The Sun Resort sits at 238 Moo 5, Don Tako, Mueang Ratchaburi, a suburban zone on the western side of Ratchaburi town, near the low hills that are the province's signature · from the resort it's a few minutes' drive to nearby highlights like the Chao Mae Kaen Chan Shrine (about 1.4 km) and Don Tako Canal (about 1.6 km), while Wat Khao Wang, the popular hilltop temple with city views, is just over 2 km away · a bit further out you'll find Khao Kaen Chan, the viewpoint with the city's Buddha image, and Khao Ngu Stone Park, the stone garden and emerald-green lake that's one of Ratchaburi's photo landmarks, both a short drive away · getting into central Ratchaburi, the old market and the train station is a quick drive too · for anyone coming from Bangkok, Ratchaburi is about 100 km away, or roughly a 1.5-hour drive, which makes it good for a weekend trip driving up for a single night · one thing worth knowing, and a point that shows up in real reviews, is that this location suits people with their own car better, because the restaurants and convenience stores around the resort aren't within an easy walk; without a car you may need to rely on hired transport or plan your meals ahead · the trade-off is an atmosphere quieter than a stay on a busy main road in town

"The room was so much cuter than the price, clean, the Wi-Fi was fast enough to take work calls, and I parked right in front of the room without circling for a spot · nice and quiet, great for a stopover, but you do need a car because there's nowhere to walk to nearby."

Room types and decor — The Sun Resort has around 37 rooms, which makes it a small resort, so it feels private and uncrowded · rooms come in several types to pick from by budget and group size, starting with the Basic room with a large bed, the cheapest entry-level option, the Standard king room, the Superior king room that's larger and more fully styled, the Twin Mountain View room for those who want a look at Ratchaburi's low hills, all the way to the 8-bed dormitory, a special draw for groups of friends or backpackers wanting to save · what gets The Sun talked about most is the loft-style decor and themed rooms that look more designed than the price — many rooms play with bare concrete walls, wooden furniture, warm-toned lighting and corners that photograph well · the praise in reviews agrees that rooms are clean, cutely styled, the beds are comfortable, and they're roomier than you'd expect for a price in the hundreds · every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, free drinking water and coffee, plus Wi-Fi that many call genuinely fast · but to be straight about it, reviews also note that because these are themed rooms, the quality and upkeep aren't equally consistent across every room — for instance, light-bulb colors that don't match within the same room, a damaged bathtub in some rooms, or too few power outlets when you need to charge several devices · on top of that, some of the smaller rooms have no window, so it's worth asking for details or looking at photos of the exact room you'll get before booking if natural light matters to you

Facilities, garden and common areas — let's be upfront from the start: The Sun Resort is a small resort with no swimming pool and no gym, so if that's what you want, this may not be the answer · what it does have, and does nicely, is a small garden and a sun terrace for sitting out with a morning or evening coffee, an easygoing atmosphere suited to a quiet stay · there are free bikes to borrow for anyone who wants to ride around the quiet, low-traffic area, a point international reviews like · the thing that earns consistent praise and is a genuine advantage is the free private parking, which is spacious enough and close to the rooms, so drivers feel at ease without hunting for a space · there are also common areas like a small cafe-and-bar corner at reception, luggage storage, and free high-speed Wi-Fi throughout, which many confirm is fast enough for online meetings or work · to sum up on facilities, The Sun is "just right" for a small budget resort — it has the essentials, focuses on cleanliness and being cute, but it isn't playing the full-facility game of a big hotel

Food and dining — The Sun Resort has a restaurant, bar and a small cafe corner on the grounds, serving Asian-style food and drinks · breakfast is a point where the information differs between platforms — some list breakfast as included, while some packages may not include it, so you should check the terms clearly when booking whether breakfast is included to avoid wrong expectations · review opinion on the food is fairly middle-of-the-road: some name the free in-room coffee and drinks as something they liked, while a few criticize that the food choices, especially vegetarian options, are still limited · because the location is in a zone where the surrounding restaurants aren't an easy walk, many choose to drive into town to eat or bring their own food · the honest tip is that if you don't have a car, plan your meals ahead or order delivery, because relying on a small resort's own kitchen for every meal may not be as convenient as a stay in town · overall, food isn't The Sun's main selling point, but it's a supporting feature that does enough for a small resort, and a location within driving distance of Ratchaburi's well-known eats helps make up for it

Service — for a small resort with few rooms, service is fairly relaxed in the style of a family-run place · many reviews mention friendly, helpful staff, especially around check-in, check-out and recommending places to see and eat in town · basic services like luggage storage, sorting out parking and daily housekeeping are handled tidily · but to be straight, the point that shows up in reviews is detail management that isn't yet consistent — some in-room items being broken and not yet repaired, or the attention to detail varying from room to room, which is the sort of thing you find in a small place that hasn't been open long and whose team isn't large yet · check-in runs roughly 14:00–23:00 and check-out roughly 08:00–12:00 · overall, service is good for the price and size of the place, and the friendliness is the charm that makes many feel comfortable staying here

What real reviews say (praise and criticism) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · on Trip.com it scores a high 8.4 (from a modest number of reviews), Booking.com sits at about 7.7 from 405 reviews, and TripAdvisor gives about 3.8 out of 5 while ranking it among the top hotels in Ratchaburi · on the praise side: rooms that are clean and cutely designed beyond the price, Wi-Fi fast enough to work or take online meetings, free in-room coffee and drinking water, free parking close to the rooms, free bikes to borrow, a quiet atmosphere, and great value for a price in the hundreds — some even say they got a lovely room at an unbelievably cheap price · on the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is the upkeep and management of the themed rooms that isn't yet consistent — mismatched bulb colors, a damaged bathtub, few outlets, and some smaller rooms with no window · next is the location that requires a car, since restaurants and convenience stores aren't within walking distance, food choices (especially vegetarian) being limited, and the uncertainty over breakfast in some packages · most of these gripes are ones you can set the right expectations for: if you understand that this is a small, budget, recently opened resort that leans on being cute and good value, not a luxury full-service stay, you'll be happy with what you get

"Only a few hundred baht but the room was prettier than I expected, the photos came out really nice, quiet and great for relaxing · the only downside was that there were too few outlets in the room, and the room I got this time had no window — next time I'll ask for the mountain-view room instead."

Price comparison and value — The Sun Resort's prices sit among the cheapest of the designed stays in Ratchaburi, with entry-level rooms in the normal range usually around THB 550–700/night, while larger or more fully styled rooms like the Superior and the mountain-view room go up with size and season, and the 8-bed dorm is priced per bed cheaper still for groups of friends or backpackers · compared with other designed stays in the province, The Sun feels great value in terms of looks for the money, since you get loft-style rooms that photograph well at a price below many boutique hotels in the town center · compared with downtown boutiques like The Bed Boutique House or Sleep by Me, which start in the low thousands, The Sun is clearly cheaper, but the trade-off is no pool, a location that needs a car, and detail upkeep that isn't as settled · in short, if the goal of your trip is to "sleep in a pretty room for an easy price, park easily, and use the stay as a base to drive around Ratchaburi," the value here is very good — but if the goal is full facilities or big-hotel service, you may have to pay more for a different option

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · one, this place suits people with a car most; if you don't have one, plan your transport and meals ahead, because the surrounding shops aren't within walking distance · two, if natural light matters to you, specify it when booking or look at room photos clearly, because some smaller rooms have no window · three, if you need to charge several devices or work, bring a power strip, because some rooms have few outlets · four, check the breakfast terms clearly when booking whether it's included, since the information differs between platforms · five, if you want a nice view choose the Twin Mountain View room, or if you're coming as a group take a look at the 8-bed dorm for better value · six, always compare prices across Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking, and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't firm, because prices for this kind of stay often shift with promotions

The verdict — from all the real reviews, The Sun Resort Ratchaburi is the stay that suits anyone who wants a pretty, designed room for an easy price, free parking and a quiet atmosphere for one or two nights while traveling around Ratchaburi · loft-themed rooms that photograph well, fast Wi-Fi, free parking close to the rooms, free bikes to borrow, and a price in the hundreds are why many say it's better value than expected and why it scores well across platforms despite only opening in 2021 · at the same time, you have to admit honestly that it's a small resort with no pool, a location that needs a car, themed-room upkeep that's uneven in places, and small details like outlets or a windowless room that are worth checking before booking · if you're after a stay with a pool and full big-hotel service, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a hotel in town or a larger resort instead · but for a trip that wants a cute room at an easy price, peace and quiet, and a base that's convenient for driving around — The Sun Resort Ratchaburi does its job well and is impressively good value for budget travelers

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — The Sun Resort Ratchaburi

faq.q: Where is The Sun Resort Ratchaburi · how do you get there?
faq.a: It's at 238 Moo 5, Don Tako, Mueang Ratchaburi, a suburban zone on the western side · near the Chao Mae Kaen Chan Shrine (~1.4 km), Don Tako Canal (~1.6 km) and Wat Khao Wang (~2.2 km) · a short drive to Khao Kaen Chan and Khao Ngu Stone Park · about a 1.5-hour drive from Bangkok · this location suits people with their own car most, because the surrounding restaurants aren't within walking distance

faq.q: How much does The Sun Resort Ratchaburi start at · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 550–700/night for the Basic and Standard rooms · there's a Superior king room, a Twin Mountain View room and an 8-bed dorm priced per bed, cheaper for groups of friends and backpackers · prices change with season and promotions, so always compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com before booking

faq.q: Who is The Sun Resort Ratchaburi best for?
faq.a: It's great for couples who want a cute room at an easy price, travelers driving their own car, and groups of friends or backpackers looking for a cheap dorm for one or two nights while traveling around Ratchaburi · it's a small boutique resort that leans on loft-style designed rooms at a budget price · if you're after a swimming pool or full big-hotel service, there may be better options in the province

faq.q: Does The Sun Resort Ratchaburi have a swimming pool and what facilities are there?
faq.a: It has no swimming pool and no gym, since it's a small resort · but there's a garden, a sun terrace, a restaurant, a bar, a cafe corner, free bikes to borrow, free private parking, and free high-speed Wi-Fi that many praise as fast enough to work and take online meetings · every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, free drinking water and coffee

faq.q: What are the things to watch out for or know about The Sun Resort Ratchaburi?
faq.a: Reviews reflect that it's a small resort that only opened in 2021, with themed-room upkeep that isn't yet consistent — mismatched bulb colors, a damaged bathtub, and few power outlets in some rooms · some smaller rooms have no window, and the location needs a car since the surrounding shops aren't walkable · we recommend looking at room photos clearly before booking, asking for a mountain-view room, and bringing your own power strip

faq.q: Does The Sun Resort Ratchaburi have a dormitory?
faq.a: Yes · it has an 8-bed dormitory priced per bed, cheaper than a private room, good for groups of friends, solo budget travelers and backpackers · it also has several private room types, from a Basic room with a large bed, Standard and Superior king rooms, to a Twin Mountain View room
